a clip of your own stays out of the backups and accepts every H.264 file; the routines copy says what the phone does; three translations put their numbers back in order.\n- **The desktop keeps up.** A failed update check is tried again within the hour; a clip of your own may be HEVC where this computer can play it, the same rule as every other device; a fragmented MP4 is read right; a release gets the installers of every platform that built, and the workflows check that every hook the chat's stylesheet leans on exists in the dsh version being staged ([#383](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/383), [#415](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/415)).\n- **The showcase and the project.** The hosted showcase believes `X-Forwarded-For` from Caddy alone, may be framed by the project's sites only, does not count a demo the box failed to start, speaks Chinese on its own pages, is built from one pinned MobileGym commit, carries health checks and says on the privacy page what it keeps ([#381](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/381), [#417](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/417)). nanoMuse 1.0.3 · Helm\n\n🐉 **nanoMuse `1.0.3` “Helm”**: the chat looks the same on every device now, a video of your own can be the face, several custom endpoints work side by side, and a day of reports from one careful tester is answered.\n\n1.0.2 went out on 2026-10-11. The same day @Ichiro786 finished a redesign of the Android app in three pull requests: the bottom bar became a floating frosted-glass pill, the chats drawer and the chat itself moved onto the theme's own canvas with black and white pills instead of blue, and the header became a soft scrim the conversation slides under ([#329](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/329), [#330](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/330), [#331](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/331)). We took that look as the reference and brought it to the iPhone, the web console and the desktop, so the five clients read as one app. @Mola-maker read the Android code and the tests and filed ten reports in an afternoon, from an own Anthropic key that could not send to a debug log that held raw API keys ([#332](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/332) to [#340](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/340), [#347](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/347)); every one of them is fixed here. Two requests became features: a clip of your own as the agent's face ([#324](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/324)) and more than one OpenAI-compatible endpoint at a time on the desktop and in the web console ([#294](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/294)). Nothing moves for a person upgrading: the Android package installs over 1.0.2 and keeps everything, the desktop keeps its settings and its one custom endpoint becomes the first of the list, and a 1.0.2 client works against the relay (0.24.2) unchanged.\n\n## Highlights\n\n- **One look on every device.** The bottom bar on Android, iPhone and the web's phone layout is a floating frosted-glass pill, as wide as the composer above it (420 at most, centred on a wider screen), icons only; the current tab shows its filled glyph on an ink disc, black in the light theme and white in the dark one, that springs across to the tab you tap. The chat is monochrome on all four clients: your messages are black pills with white text in light and white pills with black text in dark, the agent's replies sit in a pill a shade off the canvas, the send button and the scroll-to-latest disc are the same ink, the light canvas is plain white, and the header is a scrim the conversation scrolls under instead of a bar with a line. On Android the chats drawer and the menus sit on the same canvas, with a hairline edge instead of a tinted sheet ([#329](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/329), [#330](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/330), [#331](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/331) by @Ichiro786; iPhone, web and desktop follow them).\n- **A clip of your own as the face.** On Android, iPhone and the desktop the pen on the face and the avatar studio offer *Your own clip…*: the system's video picker, then a preview of the clip playing in the face's round frame with *Use* and *Cancel*. One clip, MP4 or MOV with H.264 (the iPhone also takes HEVC), at most 15 seconds and 30 MB; it plays muted in a loop for the mood at rest and stands in for every other mood, the drawn stills keep their place where a still is shown, and with no drawn face the clip's first frame is the still. The clip stays on the device that chose it, is never sent to nanoMuse Cloud and does not sync; *Default face* takes it off again. A longer, larger or differently encoded clip is refused with a sentence that states the limits ([#324](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/324), requested by @Yicheng-1218).\n- **Several custom endpoints at once.** The desktop and the web console used to hold one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so a second one could only replace the first. The custom row is a list now: each endpoint has a name, an address, its own key and its models, the picker groups the models by endpoint, and any of them can take a job. An existing single endpoint becomes the first entry without asking. The phones already worked this way ([#294](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/294), requested by @Alasco123).\n- **Ten reports on the Android app, all fixed.** An own Anthropic key sends again: the provider read the Claude Code OAuth identifier on every request, and the public build ships it empty, so every message on an own key stopped before it left the phone ([#333](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/333)). A carriage return in tool output overwrites instead of erasing, so `AAAA\\rBB` reads `BBAA` and a progress line no longer truncates the result the model sees ([#334](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/334)). Leaving the sign-in page or the network page cancels its request instead of holding the connection to the timeout ([#336](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/336)). A new set of avatar candidates no longer shows the old set's failures ([#337](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/337)). Stop right after the first message no longer saves the welcome lines as the model's reply, and puts your text back in the composer ([#340](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/340)). The debug request log masks credential headers and keeps its own copy ([#347](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/347)). Icon-only controls (the password eye, the add buttons, Like, the avatar tiles) have names for a screen reader, in all 17 languages ([#338](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/338)). And the tests: the on-device test set compiles again and CI keeps it so, the upstream provider tests feed the streams the provider actually reads, CI runs the OpenMinis provider and sandbox tests beside ours, and the runtime's web tests no longer depend on the machine's resolver ([#332](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/332), [#335](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/335), [#339](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/339)). All reported by @Mola-maker.\n- **A voice prompt from the Action Button (iPhone).** A *Voice Prompt* Shortcut opens the app and starts listening, so a prompt can be spoken instead of typed: bind it to the Action Button, Back Tap or a widget, press, speak, and the words appear in the composer; sending stays a tap. Written by @cypggs ([#298](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/298)).\n- **OpenCode Go on every client.** Go, the subscription beside Zen on the same host, asks a client to name itself and send one id per conversation; the runtime, the phones and the desktop now do, so Go is back in the own-key catalogue, and the relay's guidance lists it apart so that a 1.0.1 phone, which does not send the id, never offers it ([#325](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/325) by @PovedaAqui).\n- **A freshly installed desktop update is no longer offered to itself.** The daily update check kept its result for a day and the file outlived the update, so right after installing 1.0.2 the sidebar still said *Update to 1.0.2*; the cached result is now read against the version that runs ([#341](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/issues/341), reported by @jiangkaiqi2005).\n- **Smaller things.** The relay's Docker image runs as an unprivileged user (uid 10001) and says in one sentence what to do when its data directory is not its own; the runtime's image reports its health to `docker ps`; the unused `POST /api/avatar/estimate` is gone; every field on the web console's Connections screen is named for a screen reader; the feed's and a goal's daily time is written in plain digits on every phone; every pull request carries its platform and kind labels, and the contributor guide says plainly that an issue stays open until a maintainer closes it.\n- **TestFlight.** Build 16 (1.0.0) is what the public link installs today; builds 18 (1.0.1) and 19 (1.0.2) are still in Apple's beta review; 1.0.3 goes up as build 22 and is submitted to the same review. The link installs a build once its review has passed, the internal testers before that.\n\n## Upgrade Notes\n\n- **Android installs over 1.0.2 and keeps your data.** `nanoMuse-1.0.3-arm64.apk` (Android 8.0+, arm64; versionCode 46) is signed with the same key as every version before it. Verify with `sha256sum -c nanoMuse-1.0.3-arm64.apk.sha256`. The bottom bar, the drawer and the chat look different; nothing else moved.\n- **iPhone and iPad come through TestFlight.** The public link installs build 16 (1.0.0), which passed Apple's beta review; builds 18 and 19 are still in that review, and build 22 (1.0.3) is submitted when it is uploaded; a build reaches the link once its review has passed, the internal testers before that.\n- **The desktop installers are built by CI from `main` one commit after the tag `v1.0.3`** (the tag's Windows build failed on a test that read line endings, fixed in [#376](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/pull/376); the desktop sources are those of the tag). The Mac packages are not notarized: the first time, open the app from *System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway* (or right-click → *Open*). The Windows package is not signed: click *More info* and *Run anyway* once. On Linux prefer the `.deb`; the AppImage needs FUSE (`--appimage-extract-and-run` without). They arrive a little after the APK, and `SHA256SUMS-desktop.txt` lists every checksum. Your one custom endpoint becomes the first entry of the new list; the key stays where it was.\n- **The relay is 0.24.2; nothing changes on the wire.** A 1.0.2 client works against it unchanged. Its Docker image now runs as uid 10001, so a bind-mounted data directory must belong to that uid: `sudo chown -R 10001:10001 data` once (`scripts/self-host.sh` does it for you), and a relay that cannot write the directory says so at start instead of printing a traceback; [docs/self-hosting.md](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) has the steps.\n- **The runtime's HTTP API lost one route.** `POST /api/avatar/estimate` had no caller; everything else is as it was, and `config.toml` keeps every key it had.\n- **Where to get it.**\n\n  | | |\n  |---|---|\n  | Browser | [demo.nanomuse.dev](https://demo.nanomuse.dev/), a nanoMuse on a simulated phone, after a sign-in; a demo, the apps below are the real thing |\n  | Android 8.0+, arm64 | `nanoMuse-1.0.3-arm64.apk` |\n  | iPhone, iPad | [TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ZHexbDqc), a beta that passed Apple's review; the link installs build 16 (1.0.0) today, builds 18 (1.0.1), 19 (1.0.2) and 22 (1.0.3) once their review has passed |\n  | Windows 10+ | `nanoMuse-Desktop-1.0.3-win-x64.exe` (the desktop app, on DeepSeek Harness; not signed) |\n  | macOS 12+ | `nanoMuse-Desktop-1.0.3-mac-arm64.dmg` / `-mac-x64.dmg` (or the `.zip`: unzip, drag to Applications; not notarized) |\n  | Linux x64 | `nanoMuse-Desktop-1.0.3-linux-x64.deb` (preferred) / `.AppImage` (needs FUSE; `--appimage-extract-and-run` without) / `.tar.gz` (unpack anywhere, run `./nanomuse-desktop`) |\n  | DeepSeek Harness Desktop you already run | `dsh-nanomuse-1.0.3.tgz`, `dsh plugin --profile desktop add …` ([how](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/blob/main/harness/README.md)) |\n  | Docker | `ghcr.io/nano-muse/nanomuse:1.0.3` (also `:latest`), the runtime with the web console on port 8787 |\n  | Your own relay | `bash scripts/self-host.sh`, [docs/self-hosting.md](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md) |\n\n  In our measurements GitHub's own downloads are quick from China as well; if they fail where you are, the same files are on [nanomuse.cn/dl/v1.0.3/](https://nanomuse.cn/dl/v1.0.3/) within fifteen minutes.\n\n## Community\n\nnanoMuse is open source, free and non-profit. Sign in with a phone number or an e-mail and you get a starting allowance; the developer pays for it. The account page shows what is left and how to add more. When it is gone, use your own key or a plan you already pay for ([how](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/blob/main/docs/own-key.md)); the key you add can take over any of the four jobs, and the account can be switched off as a model source while you keep it for sync and your devices. With an account, the text of your main conversation is kept on nanoMuse Cloud so that your devices show the same chat, side chats only if you say so, and one switch in Data controls turns it off and deletes it; nothing is sold ([privacy policy](https://nanomuse.cn/privacy/)); delete the account whenever you want. The same relay runs on a server of yours: [docs/self-hosting.md](https://github.com/nano-muse/nanoMuse/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md).\n\nThis version is mostly other people's work and other people's eyes. Android、iPhone 和网页的手机布局里，底栏是一枚悬浮的毛玻璃胶囊，和上面的输入框一样宽（最宽 MB；它静音循环播放，用于待机状态，也顶替其他每种情绪，画出来的静态图在需要静态图的地方照旧，没有画过脸时用视频的第一帧当静态图。视频只留在选它的那台设备上，不上传 nanoMuse      Title: Unlimited OCR Works 
     Authors: Youyang Yin ,  Huanhuan Liu , YY,  Qunyi Xie ,  Chaorun Liu ,  Shiqi Yang ,  Shaohua Wang ,  Zhanlong Liu ,  Hao Zou ,  Jinyue Chen ,  Shu Wei ,  Jingjing Wu ,  Mingxin Huang ,  Zhen Wu ,  Guibin Wang ,  Tengyu Du ,  Lei Jia              View a PDF of the paper titled Unlimited OCR Works, by Youyang Yin and 16 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Recently, end-to-end OCR models, exemplified by DeepSeek OCR, have once again thrust OCR into the spotlight. A widely held view is that employing a large language model (LLM) as the decoder allows the model to leverage the prior distribution of language, leading to improved OCR performance. However, the downside is equally evident: as the output sequence lengthens, the accumulated KV cache drives up memory consumption and progressively slows down generation. This stands in stark contrast to humans, who exhibit no such decline in efficiency during long-horizon copying tasks. In this technical report, we propose Unlimited OCR, a model designed to emulate human parsing working memory. Taking DeepSeek OCR as the baseline, we replace all attention layers in the decoder with our proposed Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA), which reduces attention computation costs while maintaining a constant KV cache throughout the entire decoding process. By combining the high compression rate of DeepSeek OCR's encoder with our constant KV cache design, Unlimited OCR can transcribe dozens of pages of documents in a single forward pass under a standard maximum length of 32K. More importantly, R-SWA is a general-purpose parsing attention mechanism - beyond OCR, it is equally applicable to tasks such as ASR, translation, etc. Codes and model weights are publicly available at  this http URL .

## Release - [2026/07/21] 🤝 Thanks to the [ms-swift community](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) for their support, our model now supports training with [ms-swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift). - [2026/07/03] 🤝 Thanks to the Baidu Cloud team for their support. Our model is now available on [Baidu Cloud](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/OCR/s/fmr1p39gb). - [2026/06/28] 🤝 Thanks to the [vLLM community](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) and [Tianyu Guo](https://github.com/gty111) for their support, our model now supports vLLM inference. - [2026/06/24] 🤝 Thanks to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for creating a demo for us. It is now available at [Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/23] 📄 Our paper is now available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23050). - [2026/06/23] 🤝 Thanks to the [ModelScope community](https://github.com/modelscope) for their support. Our model is now available at [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/PaddlePaddle/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/22] 🚀 We present [Unlimited-OCR](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR), aiming to push [Deepseek-OCR](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR) one step further. ## Inference ### Transformers Inference using Huggingface transformers on NVIDIA GPUs. Requirements tested on python 3.12.3 + CUDA12.9： ``` torch==2.10.0 torchvision==0.25.0 transformers==4.57.1 Pillow==12.1.1 matplotlib==3.10.8 einops==0.8.2 addict==2.4.0 easydict==1.13 pymupdf==1.27.2.2 psutil==7.2.2 ``` ```python import os import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer model_name = 'baidu/Unlimited-OCR' tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained( model_name, trust_remote_code=True, use_safetensors=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ) model = model.eval().cuda() # ── Single image supports two configs: gundam or base ── # gundam: base_size=1024, image_size=640, crop_mode=True # base: base_size=1024, image_size=1024, crop_mode=False model.infer( tokenizer, prompt='document parsing.', image_file='your_image.jpg', output_path='your/output/dir', base_size=1024, image_size=640, crop_mode=True, max_length=32768, no_repeat_ngram_size=35, ngram_window=128, save_results=True, ) # ── Multi page / PDF only uses base (image_size=1024) ── model.infer_multi( tokenizer, prompt='Multi page parsing.', image_files=['page1.png', 'page2.png', 'page3.png'], output_path='your/output/dir', image_size=1024, max_length=32768, no_repeat_ngram_size=35, ngram_window=1024, save_results=True, ) # ── PDF (convert pages to images, then multi-page parsing) ── import tempfile, fitz # PyMuPDF def pdf_to_images(pdf_path, dpi=300): doc = fitz.open(pdf_path) tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='pdf_ocr_') mat = fitz.Matrix(dpi / 72, dpi / 72) paths = [] for i, page in enumerate(doc): out = os.path.join(tmp_dir, f'page_{i+1:04d}.png') page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat).save(out) paths.append(out) doc.close() return paths model.infer_multi( tokenizer, prompt='Multi page parsing.', image_files=pdf_to_images('your_doc.pdf', dpi=300), output_path='your/output/dir', image_size=1024, max_length=32768, no_repeat_ngram_size=35, ngram_window=1024, save_results=True, ) ``` ### vLLM Please refer to the official vLLM recipe for deployment details: **Recipe:** [https://recipes.vllm.ai/baidu/Unlimited-OCR](https://recipes.vllm.ai/baidu/Unlimited-OCR) ##### Docker Images Use the following Docker images depending on your GPU platform: **Default (CUDA 13.0):** ```bash docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr ``` **For Hopper GPUs (CUDA 12.9)** ```bash docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr-cu129 ``` ### SGLang Set up the environment (uv-managed virtualenv). Install the local SGLang wheel first, then pin `kernels==0.9.0` and install PyMuPDF for PDF-to-image conversion: ```shell uv venv --python 3.12 source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install wheel/sglang-0.0.0.dev11416+g92e8bb79e-py3-none-any.whl uv pip install kernels==0.11.7 uv pip install pymupdf==1.27.2.2 ``` Start the SGLang server: ```shell python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model baidu/Unlimited-OCR \ --served-model-name Unlimited-OCR \ --attention-backend fa3 \ --page-size 1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \ --context-length 32768 \ --enable-custom-logit-processor \ --disable-overlap-schedule \ --skip-server-warmup \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 10000 ``` Send streaming requests to the OpenAI-compatible API: ```python import base64 import json import os import tempfile import fitz import requests from sglang.srt.sampling.custom_logit_processor import DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor server_url = "http://127.0.0.1:10000" session = requests.Session() session.trust_env = False def pdf_to_images(pdf_path, dpi=300): doc = fitz.open(pdf_path) tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pdf_ocr_") mat = fitz.Matrix(dpi / 72, dpi / 72) image_paths = [] for i, page in enumerate(doc): image_path = os.path.join(tmp_dir, f"page_{i + 1:04d}.png") page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat).save(image_path) image_paths.append(image_path) doc.close() return image_paths def encode_image(image_path): ext = os.path.splitext(image_path)[1].lower() mime = "image/jpeg" if ext in (".jpg", ".jpeg") else f"image/{ext.lstrip('.')}" with open(image_path, "rb") as f: data = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8") return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:{mime};base64,{data}"}} def build_content(prompt, image_paths): return [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}] + [encode_image(path) for path in image_paths] def generate(prompt, image_paths, image_mode, ngram_window): payload = { "model": "Unlimited-OCR", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": build_content(prompt, image_paths)}], "temperature": 0, "skip_special_tokens": False, "images_config": {"image_mode": image_mode}, "custom_logit_processor": DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor.to_str(), "custom_params": { "ngram_size": 35, "window_size": ngram_window, }, "stream": True, } response = session.post( f"{server_url}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, data=json.dumps(payload), timeout=1200, stream=True, ) response.raise_for_status() chunks = [] for line in response.iter_lines(chunk_size=1, decode_unicode=True): if not line or not line.startswith("data: "): continue data = line[len("data: "):] if data == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(data) delta = event["choices"][0].get("delta", {}).get("content", "") if delta: print(delta, end="", flush=True) chunks.append(delta) print() return "".join(chunks) # Single image supports two configs: gundam or base. Example below uses gundam. generate("document parsing.", ["your_image.jpg"], image_mode="gundam", ngram_window=128) # Multi image (base only) generate("Multi page parsing.", ["page1.png", "page2.png"], image_mode="base", ngram_window=1024) # PDF (base only) generate("Multi page parsing.", pdf_to_images("your_doc.pdf", dpi=300), image_mode="base", ngram_window=1024) ``` For batch inference, `infer.py` starts the SGLang server automatically and sends concurrent requests for an image directory or PDF: ```shell # Image directory python infer.py \ --image_dir ./examples/images \ --output_dir ./outputs \ --concurrency 8 \ --image_mode gundam # PDF pages python infer.py \ --pdf ./examples/document.pdf \ --output_dir ./outputs \ --concurrency 8 \ --image_mode gundam ``` Useful options: ```shell --model_dir baidu/Unlimited-OCR # Local path or Hugging Face model ID --gpu 0 # CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value --server_log ./log/sglang_server.log ``` For OmniDocBench evaluation, you need to perform the following post-processing. ```python DET_RE = re.compile(r'<\|det\|>([^<\s]+)(?:\s*\[[^\]]*\])?\s*<\|/det\|>(.*)', re.DOTALL) def remove_det(raw: str) -> str: """ Strip <|det|>type [bbox]<|/det|> markers, group lines belonging to the same block with \\n, and separate different blocks with \\n\\n.      Title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning 
     Authors: Linhao Zhong ,  Bozhen Fang ,  Xuehao Wang ,  Duochao Shi ,  Zekai Luo ,  Guangming Yao ,  Yi Yuan ,  Hao Chen ,  Jingdong Chen ,  Chunhua Shen              View a PDF of the paper titled More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning, by Linhao Zhong and 9 other authors 
     View PDF 



     
             Abstract: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods. Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison. To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods. Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, gains over GRPO remain limited in scope, with no method consistently outperforming it across settings. Second, strong final performance can mask unstable training. Third, additional training cost does not consistently translate into better performance. We establish this benchmark to support fair, comprehensive comparison and guide future research toward reliable and cost-effective improvements in agent training. # More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2610.19789-b31b1b)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19789) [![Project](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Page-blue)](https://aim-uofa.github.io/Self-Distillation-AgentRL) [![Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Code-GitHub-orange)](https://github.com/aim-uofa/Self-Distillation-AgentRL)
**Self-Distillation-AgentRL** is the official codebase for our study of self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning. ## Overview Do more self-distillation methods lead to better agents? We compare ten representative approaches against GRPO across four benchmarks and three model sizes, using shared environments and evaluation procedures while retaining method-specific training settings. Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost. ![Study overview: limitations of prior comparisons and a unified benchmark across methods, tasks, and model sizes.](assets/overview.png) **Study overview.** From fragmented evidence to a common benchmark for assessing the breadth of gains, training stability, and computational cost. Our evaluation yields three main findings: - **Gains remain setting-dependent.** No method consistently outperforms GRPO across settings. - **Strong final performance does not imply stable training.** Final scores can conceal instability along the training trajectory. - **More computation does not consistently yield better agents.** Additional training cost does not reliably translate into improved performance. This repository provides a common framework for training, checkpoint conversion, and evaluation, supporting direct comparisons and further research on reliable, cost-effective agent training. ## Benchmark Coverage The study spans **12 model–task settings** and **132 training runs**, with repeated evaluations over **eight rollout seeds** for pretrained and trained models. ### Supported Models - ✅ Qwen3.5-2B (`MODEL_SIZE=2B`) - ✅ Qwen3.5-4B (`MODEL_SIZE=4B`) - ✅ Qwen3.5-9B (`MODEL_SIZE=9B`) ### Supported Benchmarks - ✅ ALFWorld (`TASK=alfworld`) - ✅ ScienceWorld (`TASK=scienceworld`) - ✅ Search-QA (`TASK=search`) - ✅ WebShop (`TASK=webshop`) ### Supported Methods - ✅ GRPO — baseline (`METHOD=grpo`) - ✅ GRPO+OPSD (`METHOD=grpo_opsd`) - ✅ SDAR (`METHOD=sdar`) - ✅ Skill-SD (`METHOD=skillsd`) - ✅ RLSD (`METHOD=rlsd`) - ✅ OCSD (`METHOD=ocsd`) - ✅ OVCSD (`METHOD=ovcsd`) - ✅ AgentOPSD (`METHOD=agentopsd`) - ✅ ADRS (`METHOD=adrs`) - ✅ ICSD (`METHOD=icsd`) - ✅ PCSD (`METHOD=pcsd`) The launchers support training-time validation, standalone evaluation, rollout recording, benchmark mean/standard deviation, and pass@k. ## Getting Started All entry points are in [launchers/](launchers/). The workflow below covers environment setup, data preparation, training, checkpoint conversion, and evaluation. ### 1. Environment Setup Use Linux x86_64 with Conda, NVIDIA GPUs, and a compatible CUDA toolchain/C++ compiler. Run all commands in Bash from the repository root. ```bash chmod +x launchers/*.sh export PROJECT_ROOT="$(dirname "$PWD")" export CONDA_ENV=agentrl export DATA_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT/data" export HF_HOME="$PROJECT_ROOT/hf_cache" export VERL_AUTO_PADDING=1 bash launchers/setup_env.sh source launchers/conda.sh agentrl_activate_conda ``` The installer creates the environment, installs the local packages and pinned dependencies, and applies the bundled decord/TextWorld compatibility wheels automatically. Dependency specifications are in [requirements.txt](requirements.txt), [requirements-kernels.txt](requirements-kernels.txt), and [constraints.txt](constraints.txt). Choose an unused `CONDA_ENV`; use `REUSE_ENV=1` only to resume an interrupted installation. If Conda is not detected, set `CONDA_BASE` to its installation directory. In new terminals, repeat the exports and activation commands, not the installation. Models, data, logs, and checkpoints default to `$PROJECT_ROOT`. ### 2. Models and Data Choose `2B`, `4B`, or `9B` for `MODEL_SIZE` and download the corresponding model: ```bash export MODEL_SIZE=2B export MODEL_PATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/models/Qwen3.5-${MODEL_SIZE}" MODEL_ID="Qwen/Qwen3.5-${MODEL_SIZE}" bash launchers/prepare_model.sh ``` For an existing local model, set `MODEL_SIZE` and `MODEL_PATH` and skip the download. Interrupted downloads resume with the same command. When switching models, update these variables and regenerate `EXPERIMENT_NAME` below. Prepare only the benchmarks you need: ```bash bash launchers/prepare_alfworld.sh bash launchers/prepare_webshop.sh small bash launchers/prepare_search.sh qa bash launchers/prepare_search.sh retrieval bash launchers/install_scienceworld.sh bash launchers/prepare_scienceworld.sh ``` For Search-QA, start the retrieval service in a second terminal with the same environment and path exports: ```bash GPU_ID=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 PORT=19080 FAISS_GPU=1 \ bash launchers/start_search_retriever.sh ``` This shards the FAISS index across GPUs 0–7 in FP16 and runs the E5 encoder on GPU 0. Keep the service running and reserve memory for it when sharing GPUs with training or evaluation. In each training/evaluation terminal, set the retrieval endpoint: ```bash export SEARCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:19080/retrieve ``` Update `SEARCH_URL` if you change the service host or port. ### 3. Training Choose `METHOD` and `TASK` from the identifiers in [Benchmark Coverage](#benchmark-coverage). The same command works across the supported models, methods, and benchmarks; `PAPER_CONFIG=1` selects the study-oriented launcher defaults. ```bash export METHOD=grpo TASK=alfworld export EXPERIMENT_NAME="${METHOD}_qwen35_${MODEL_SIZE,,}_${TASK}_8gpu" GPU_ID=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 PAPER_CONFIG=1 \ TOTAL_TRAINING_STEPS=100 TEST_FREQ=5 \ SAVE_FREQ=20 MAX_ACTOR_CKPTS=5 RESUME_MODE=disable \ bash "launchers/train_${METHOD}_${TASK}.sh" \ trainer.n_gpus_per_node=8 ray_init.num_cpus=64 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=True \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enforce_eager=False \ +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.gdn_prefill_backend=triton ``` Keep `GPU_ID` and `trainer.n_gpus_per_node` consistent; for one GPU, use `GPU_ID=0` and `trainer.n_gpus_per_node=1`. To resume training, keep the original experiment name and set `RESUME_MODE=auto`. With `PAPER_CONFIG=1`, rollout GPU memory utilization defaults to 0.30 for 2B/4B training, 0.65 for 9B training (including validation), and 0.30 for standalone evaluation. Model size is selected by `MODEL_SIZE`, or the standard model directory name when unset. Override with `GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION` if needed. ### 4. Checkpoint Conversion Convert a saved checkpoint to Hugging Face format before evaluation. Change `global_step_100` to select a different training step. ```bash CHECKPOINT_TASK="$TASK" if [[ "$TASK" == search ]]; then CHECKPOINT_TASK=searchQA; fi STEP_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/checkpoints/$METHOD/$CHECKPOINT_TASK/$EXPERIMENT_NAME/global_step_100" bash "launchers/merge_${METHOD}_checkpoint.sh" "$STEP_DIR" export MERGED_MODEL="$STEP_DIR/merged_hf" ``` Allow enough CPU RAM and disk space for merging; evaluation uses `merged_hf/`, not the raw `actor/` shards. ### 5. Evaluation To evaluate pretrained weights, complete steps 1–2 and select a benchmark, for example `export TASK=alfworld`. To evaluate a trained checkpoint, first convert it as described above. #### Single Evaluation ```bash PAPER_CONFIG=1 GPU_ID=0 EVAL_DO_SAMPLE=true EVAL_TEMPERATURE=0.4 \ bash "launchers/test_pretrained_${TASK}.sh" \ ray_init.num_cpus=64 \ +actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.model_dtype=bfloat16 \ actor_rollout_ref.rollout.enable_chunked_prefill=True \ +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.gdn_prefill_backend=triton ``` To evaluate a trained model, use `bash "launchers/test_${METHOD}_${TASK}.sh" "$MERGED_MODEL"` in place of the pretrained script, keeping the same environment variables and overrides. #### Multiple Seeds and Pass@k ```bash PAPER_CONFIG=1 MODEL_KIND=pretrained GPU_IDS=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \ MAX_PASS_K=8 TEMPERATURE=0.4 \ RUN_ID=eval_run_01 \ bash launchers/eval_pass_at_k.sh ``` For a merged checkpoint from any method, replace `MODEL_KIND=pretrained` with `MODEL_KIND=grpo GRPO_MODEL_PATH="$MERGED_MODEL" MODEL_TAG="${EXPERIMENT_NAME}_step100"`. Here `grpo` names the shared checkpoint-loading route, not the training method; adjust the tag to match the checkpoint step. With `MAX_PASS_K=8`, seeds default to 0–7, with one seed per GPU. Logs are saved under `$PROJECT_ROOT/logs/`. Repeated evaluation also saves rollouts, benchmark mean/standard deviation, and pass@k under `logs/pass_at_k/`. ## Acknowledgments Our implementation builds on [SDAR](https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/SDAR), [veRL](https://github.com/volcengine/verl), and [verl-agent](https://github.com/langfengQ/verl-agent).      Title: Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models 
     Authors: Glenn Jocher ,  Jing Qiu ,  Mengyu Liu ,  Shuai Lyu ,  Fatih Cagatay Akyon ,  Muhammet Esat Kalfaoglu              View a PDF of the paper titled Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models, by Glenn Jocher and 5 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Real-time vision demands models that are accurate, efficient, and simple to deploy across diverse hardware. The YOLO family has become widely deployed for this reason, yet most YOLO detectors still rely on non-maximum suppression at inference, carry heavy detection heads due to Distribution Focal Loss, require long training schedules, and can leave the smallest objects without positive label assignments. We present Ultralytics YOLO26, a unified real-time vision model family that addresses these limitations through coordinated architecture and training advances. YOLO26 uses a dual-head design for native NMS-free end-to-end inference and removes DFL entirely, yielding a lighter head with unconstrained regression range. Its training pipeline combines MuSGD, a hybrid Muon-SGD optimizer adapted from large language model training; Progressive Loss, which shifts supervision toward the inference-time head; and STAL, a label assignment strategy that guarantees positive coverage for small objects. Beyond detection, YOLO26 introduces task-specific head and loss designs for instance segmentation, pose estimation, and oriented detection, producing consistent gains across tasks and scales. The family spans five scales (n/s/m/l/x) and supports detection, instance segmentation, pose estimation, classification, and oriented detection in a single pipeline, with an open-vocabulary extension, YOLOE-26, for text-, visual-, and prompt-free inference. Across all scales, YOLO26 achieves 40.9-57.5 mAP on COCO at 1.7-11.8 ms T4 TensorRT latency, advancing the accuracy-latency Pareto front over prior real-time detectors, while YOLOE-26x reaches 40.6 AP on LVIS minival under text prompting. Code and models are available at  this https URL .

[Ultralytics](https://www.ultralytics.com) creates cutting-edge, state-of-the-art (SOTA) [YOLO models](https://www.ultralytics.com/yolo) built on years of foundational research in computer vision and AI. Constantly updated for performance and flexibility, our models are **fast**, **accurate**, and **easy to use**. They excel at [object detection](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/detect), [instance segmentation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/segment), [semantic segmentation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/semantic), [depth estimation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/depth), [image classification](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/classify), [pose estimation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/pose), and [oriented object detection](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/obb) tasks, and can [track](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/track) detected objects across video frames. Find detailed documentation in the [Ultralytics Docs](https://docs.ultralytics.com). Get support via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/issues/new/choose). Join discussions on [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/ultralytics), [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/ultralytics/), and the [Ultralytics Community Forums](https://community.ultralytics.com)! Request an Enterprise License for commercial use at [Ultralytics Licensing](https://www.ultralytics.com/license).
## 📄 Documentation See below for quickstart installation and usage examples. For comprehensive guidance on training, validation, prediction, and deployment, refer to our full [Ultralytics Docs](https://docs.ultralytics.com).
Install Install the `ultralytics` package, including all [requirements](https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/blob/main/pyproject.toml), in a [**Python>=3.8**](https://www.python.org/) environment with [**PyTorch>=1.8**](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/). [![PyPI - Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/ultralytics?logo=pypi&logoColor=white)](https://pypi.org/project/ultralytics/) [![Ultralytics Downloads](https://static.pepy.tech/badge/ultralytics)](https://clickpy.clickhouse.com/dashboard/ultralytics) [![PyPI - Python Version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/ultralytics?logo=python&logoColor=gold)](https://pypi.org/project/ultralytics/) ```bash pip install ultralytics ``` For alternative installation methods, including [Conda](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/ultralytics), [Docker](https://hub.docker.com/r/ultralytics/ultralytics), and building from source via Git, please consult the [Quickstart Guide](https://docs.ultralytics.com/quickstart). [![Conda Version](https://img.shields.io/conda/vn/conda-forge/ultralytics?logo=condaforge)](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/ultralytics) [![Docker Image Version](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/ultralytics/ultralytics?sort=semver&logo=docker)](https://hub.docker.com/r/ultralytics/ultralytics) [![Ultralytics Docker Pulls](https://img.shields.io/docker/pulls/ultralytics/ultralytics?logo=docker)](https://hub.docker.com/r/ultralytics/ultralytics)
Usage ### CLI You can use Ultralytics YOLO directly from the Command Line Interface (CLI) with the `yolo` command: ```bash # Predict using a pretrained YOLO model (e.g., YOLO26n) on an image yolo predict model=yolo26n.pt source='https://ultralytics.com/images/bus.jpg' ``` The `yolo` command supports various tasks and modes, accepting additional arguments like `imgsz=640`. Explore the YOLO [CLI Docs](https://docs.ultralytics.com/usage/cli) for more examples. ### Python Ultralytics YOLO can also be integrated directly into your Python projects. It accepts the same [configuration arguments](https://docs.ultralytics.com/usage/cfg) as the CLI: ```python from ultralytics import YOLO # Load a pretrained YOLO26n model model = YOLO("yolo26n.pt") # Train the model on the COCO8 dataset for 100 epochs train_results = model.train( data="coco8.yaml", # Path to dataset configuration file epochs=100, # Number of training epochs imgsz=640, # Image size for training device="cpu", # Device to run on (e.g., 'cpu', 0, [0,1,2,3]) ) # Evaluate the model's performance on the validation set metrics = model.val() # Perform object detection on an image results = model("path/to/image.jpg") # Predict on an image results[0].show() # Display results # Export the model to ONNX format for deployment path = model.export(format="onnx") # Returns the path to the exported model ``` Discover more examples in the YOLO [Python Docs](https://docs.ultralytics.com/usage/python).
## ✨ Models > **[YOLO27 — Coming Soon](https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo27/):** Preview the upcoming family, currently undergoing final R&D. Models are not yet available, and no launch date is set. Ultralytics supports a wide range of YOLO models, from early versions like [YOLOv3](https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolov3) to the latest [YOLO26](https://docs.ultralytics.com/models/yolo26). The tables below showcase YOLO26 models pretrained on [COCO](https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/detect/coco) for [Detection](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/detect), [Segmentation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/segment), and [Pose Estimation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/pose). [Semantic Segmentation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/semantic) models are pretrained on [Cityscapes](https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/semantic/cityscapes), [Depth Estimation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/depth) models are pretrained on a broad multi-dataset mix and evaluated on [NYU Depth V2](https://cs.nyu.edu/~fergus/datasets/nyu_depth_v2.html), [Classification](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/classify) models are pretrained on [ImageNet](https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/classify/imagenet), and [OBB](https://docs.ultralytics.com/tasks/obb) models are pretrained on [DOTAv1](https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/obb/dota-v2#dota-v10). [Tracking](https://docs.ultralytics.com/modes/track) mode is compatible with Detection, Segmentation, Pose, and OBB models.  🌟 Summary
Release **v8.4.178** makes Platform training links more reliable and brings a broad set of fixes for model validation, tracking, exports, data loading, and training integrations. It also adds a cross-domain benchmark resource and expands Platform documentation.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Reliable Platform training links (PR #26699):** Training now prints the model URL returned by the server, which knows the final owner, project, and model name. This avoids broken links when those details differ from the local training arguments; if the server provides no URL, no link is printed.
- **Broader model evaluation:** A new Ultralytics Benchmark page describes a fixed evaluation protocol across 37 real-world detection datasets, spanning areas such as medical imaging, retail, industry, and aerial imagery. The YOLO27 documentation also updates its reported performance figures and links to the benchmark.
- **Model and tracking compatibility:** YOLO-NAS receives fixes for loading by model name, prediction, validation, export, and ReID tracking. FastSAM prompts now persist across later images and video frames; SAM tracking preserves object IDs when masks are blank; and oriented-box tracking handles equivalent box representations more consistently.
- **More dependable validation and exports:** Validation now respects non-square input shapes recorded in static exports. Fixes also address TorchScript loading on Apple MPS, dynamic ONNX execution on MPS, and full-integer LiteRT/TensorFlow input handling.
- **Platform reporting improvements:** Validation curves now better match segmentation and pose results, and class labels stay aligned when validation data omits classes. Confusion-matrix logging is corrected for Comet and DVC, including cases where no matrix is available.
- **Training and workflow reliability:** TensorBoard writers close cleanly after training, FP32 optimizer momentum is retained in checkpoints, Ascend NPU training avoids an unsupported reduction, and Docker publishing skips overwriting tags with images built from newer commits.
- **Platform and documentation updates:** Platform guides document paid annotation and image-generation models, new Explore filters, and AI-assisted training diagnosis. Other fixes improve UTF-8 dataset and source-manifest reading, screenshot inputs, ZIP naming, and CLI error messages.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Platform users** get working model links and clearer, more accurate training results.
- **Developers** benefit from more consistent behavior across model families, trackers, export formats, and hardware backends.
- **Teams managing experiments and data** get safer Docker releases, cleaner training teardown, and fewer failures caused by encoding, file naming, or configuration-directory issues.
- **Model evaluators** gain a broader reference for comparing performance beyond COCO; the benchmark results are documentation and evaluation resources, not a new model architecture in this release.

## What's Changed
* Skip Docker pushes over images built from newer commits by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26666
* Send Platform curve row class indices when val lacks classes by @JaviChulvi in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26665
* List every Platform class-prompted annotation model by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26668
* Show plain CLI argument errors and skip callables in suggestions by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26675
* Document paid image generation models in Ultralytics Platform by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26683
* Fix Comet confusion matrix orientation and labels by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26669
* Send the task's own validation curves to Platform for segment and pose by @JaviChulvi in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26678
* Fix FastSAM prompts on later frames and keep SAM2 object ids as classes by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26676
* Document new explore filters, diagnose with ai and platform api details by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26677
* Fix YOLO-NAS export, loading by name and ReID tracking by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26670

# 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.177 makes SAM prompts work consistently across image directories and video frames, alongside fixes that improve export reliability, training resumes, and prediction inputs.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- **SAM prompts now persist across a source:** Prompts supplied for a directory or video are applied to every image or frame, rather than just the first. Prompt coordinates are also scaled without changing caller-owned NumPy arrays or tensors.
- **More reliable model exports and inference:** Dynamic OpenVINO exports are pinned to the requested image size on Intel NPUs, which require fixed input dimensions. ONNX GPU inference now falls back to a compatible execution path when output shapes contain symbolic dimensions.
- **Safer training and checkpoint recovery:** Short training runs now take an optimizer step instead of potentially ending without updating the model. RMSprop checkpoints preserve small gradient-history values, helping resumed training avoid unexpectedly large updates.
- **More consistent prediction inputs:** PIL images now respect EXIF orientation, and source lists download only actual HTTP(S) URLs—so local paths beginning with `http` are not mistaken for links.
- **Improved experiment tracking and integrations:** Integration settings are read for each training run. W&B fixes improve final plot logging, offline resume IDs, project/run naming, and cleanup after interrupted or failed runs.
- **Documentation and workflow updates:** Guides clarify validation image geometry, W&B usage, Platform export options, and contribution testing advice. CI failure alerts are centralized, and runner images regain dependencies needed for Codecov signature checks.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **SAM users** can provide prompts once and get the intended segmentation behavior throughout a folder or video, whether using Python, streaming, or the CLI.
- **Training and deployment users** should see fewer failures on Intel NPUs and dynamic-output ONNX models, while checkpoint resumes and very short runs behave more reliably.
- **Everyday prediction workflows** handle phone-camera images and mixed source lists more predictably.
- **No new model architecture is introduced** in this release; the emphasis is on more dependable prediction, training, export, integrations, and documentation.

## What's Changed
* Name Platform export options and update the contributing guide's test advice by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26659

 🌟 Summary
YOLO 8.4.176 makes YOLO-World checkpoints much smaller after setting custom classes, while improving reliability across validation, fine-tuning, segmentation, tracking, and model deployment.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **YOLO-World checkpoints are dramatically smaller:** Setting classes no longer caches the CLIP text encoder by default. For `yolov8s-worldv2.pt`, a saved checkpoint shrank from **328.5 MB to 25.8 MB**, with identical predictions after reload. Caching remains available when explicitly requested.
- **More reliable validation and fine-tuning:** Detection validation now matches predictions to eligible targets in confidence order, reducing missed matches. YOLOE fine-tuning and resume also preserve trained classification heads instead of reinitializing them.
- **Fixes for segmentation and SAM:** MobileSAM FP16 inference no longer produces empty masks. Reused SAM predictors now reset state for new images and videos. A mask-thresholding change was reverted after it reduced YOLO26 segmentation mAP.
- **Improved deployment and input handling:** ONNX GPU inference now supports custom input names and strided tensors; OpenVINO NPU inference handles batches and depth outputs more reliably. Floating-point NumPy images also work with grayscale models.
- **Smoother video, tracking, and benchmarking:** Saved videos preserve fractional frame rates, high-FPS streams are handled correctly, and trackers can be copied or pickled on newer Python versions. Several benchmark workflow issues were fixed.
- **Documentation and Platform updates:** Docs clarify fine-tuning, inference, and precision behavior; Platform documentation covers relevance-based dataset sorting, email changes, and AI-assisted model comparison.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Save storage and simplify sharing:** YOLO-World users can save and move custom-vocabulary checkpoints without carrying an unnecessary CLIP encoder.
- **Trust results and continue training safely:** Validation matching and YOLOE resume fixes reduce misleading evaluation results and prevent trained heads from being lost.
- **Get more dependable inference across devices:** SAM, ONNX, OpenVINO, image inputs, and video handling work more consistently across common workflows.
- **Keep segmentation metrics stable:** Reverting the mask threshold avoids the measured mAP regression introduced by the earlier change.

     Title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction 
     Authors: Hanchen Xia ,  Baoyou Chen ,  Yutang Ge ,  Naihao Deng ,  Senqiao Yang ,  Zilong Dong ,  Weihao Yuan ,  Siyu Zhu              View a PDF of the paper titled REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction, by Hanchen Xia and 6 other authors 
     View PDF 
     HTML (experimental) 



     
             Abstract: Long-horizon agents compact their history to continue within a finite context window, but a textual summary alone may not support every subsequent decision. We introduce REMORY, a neural memory network that supplements the summary with a bounded sequence of soft memory tokens. Given the history and summary, the network learns to generate tokens that help a frozen LLM approximate the continuation it would produce with the full history. The tokens are conditioned on the summary and appended after it, forming an analogue of a residual connection along the sequence dimension. On SummHay, REMORY improves source attribution at nearly unchanged insight coverage and approaches the full-context joint score using only 5.2% of the input positions. Across long-horizon agent benchmarks, Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash show consistent gains with residual memory. Both models also exhibit substantially fewer repeated tool outputs and tool errors on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

# Remory: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction **Remory** supplements an agent's compaction summary with learned soft memory from its history. The memory is conditioned on the summary and appended after it, helping the frozen model continue its work across compactions. [📄 **Paper**](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.11287) | [💻 **Code**](https://github.com/1ring2rta/Remory) | [🤗 **Models**](#models) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca8f59f1-45c2-46e6-8261-463c8c5f21d3 Music: Electric Dreams by Scott Buckley · CC BY 4.0 · Credits & edit details ![Remory: summary-conditioned residual memory alongside standard Codex compaction, with training curves from the paper.](assets/remory.png) ## Models | Base model | Memory checkpoint | Deployment | | --- | --- | --- | | Qwen3.8-27B | [Qwen3.8-27B-REMORY-1.9B](https://huggingface.co/mocoV3/Qwen3.8-27B-REMORY-1.9B) | [SGLang](docs/deployment.md#launch), [Transformers](docs/deployment.md#transformers) | | GLM-5.3-Flash | [GLM-5.3-Flash-REMORY-1.24B](https://huggingface.co/mocoV3/GLM-5.3-Flash-REMORY-1.24B) | [SGLang](docs/deployment.md#glm-53-flash) | The GLM release is the 1.24B checkpoint used in local evaluations, distinct from the 1.502B encoder described in the paper. Both models use the same pinned SGLang version and launcher. The quick start below uses Qwen. ## Quick Start Plan for **at least 2 × 80 GB GPUs** to deploy **Qwen3.8-27B + Remory** with SGLang. The command below loads both models and serves generation and compaction through one endpoint. See [deployment](docs/deployment.md) for more options. ### 1. Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/1ring2rta/Remory.git cd Remory python deploy/install.py source .remory/venv/bin/activate ``` The installer prepares a local environment with the pinned SGLang version, Remory hook, and CUDA compiler components. ### 2. Launch SGLang with Remory ```bash CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 python -m remory.launch_server \ --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \ --remory-checkpoint mocoV3/Qwen3.8-27B-REMORY-1.9B \ --tp 2 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8421 ``` `--tp 2` splits the LLM across the two GPUs; each worker also loads Remory. The context window defaults to the model maximum (256K for Qwen3.8-27B). The first run downloads weights and compiles GPU kernels. For an existing clone, follow the [upgrade instructions](docs/deployment.md#upgrade). The launcher downloads the pinned checkpoint automatically. ### 3. Open Codex In another terminal: ```bash source .remory/venv/bin/activate r-codex -C /path/to/project ``` This opens the native Codex UI with Remory compaction. Use `/compact` during a session and `r-codex resume --last` to return later. Codex is installed on first use. See [Codex](integrations/codex) for sessions, sub-agents, and MCP tools. For the research demo's web search and document tools, enable `--research-tools`. This requires **`SERPER_API_KEY`** and **`MINERU_API_KEY`** (`MINERU_API_TOKEN` is also accepted), plus the separate Docling/MinerU tool environment. Run `r-codex tools` to check your setup. See [research tools and API keys](integrations/codex/README.md#research-tools-and-api-keys) for installation and configuration; local chat and shell/file tools need no external API key. ### Generate and compact through the API ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8421/generate \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"text":"The capital of France is", "sampling_params":{"temperature":0,"max_new_tokens":16}}' ``` In another terminal, run the full compaction example from the repository root: ```bash source .remory/venv/bin/activate python examples/quickstart.py ``` The example generates an answer, creates a summary and residual memory, then continues from that checkpoint. All model calls use the same SGLang `/generate` endpoint. During residual encoding, the Remory hook reads the actor's hidden states and runs the memory network. During continuation, it inserts the saved soft tokens after the summary. ## Replace compact [`Harness.compact`](src/remory/adapters/harness.py) is the compaction method to connect to your agent: generate a summary, encode residual memory, then return the new checkpoint. The agent retains its own tools and compaction trigger. ```python from remory.adapters import Harness from remory.client import Client with Client("http://127.0.0.1:8421", session_id="my-session") as client: agent = Harness(client, codec) # The actor's native chat template checkpoint = agent.compact( prefix_messages=prefix, # System prompt, tools, and original task removed_messages=history, summary_prompt=summary_prompt, summary_schema=summary_schema, ) result = agent.generate( checkpoint=checkpoint, prefix_messages=prefix, messages=new_messages, ) ``` The [complete example](examples/quickstart.py) loads the tokenizer and summary prompt from the released checkpoint. If your harness already generates a summary, use `on_compact(..., summary=summary)` to add residual memory. Save the checkpoint with the conversation. For the next compaction, pass it as `previous` and supply the newly removed history. Memory is stored in `.remory/memory.sqlite`. The [Codex integration](integrations/codex) provides a complete Responses provider and an interactive launcher. See the [API reference](docs/api.md) for native SGLang requests with memory. ## Training The [Qwen3.8-27B training guide](training) includes the Stage I reconstruction trainer, Stage II summary-conditioned residual-memory trainer, four-GPU launch commands, and checkpoint/resume instructions. Both stages freeze Qwen and train only the memory network. [Synthetic JSONL examples](training/examples) show the document and history/summary/continuation formats, with CPU preparation commands. ## Results ![BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1 scores for Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash, with and without residual memory.](assets/benchmarks.png) Qwen3.8-27B and GLM-5.3-Flash improve across long-horizon agent benchmarks. Residual memory also reduces repeated tool outputs and tool errors on BrowseComp and Terminal-Bench 2.1. On SummHay, it approaches the full-context joint score using 5.2% of the input positions. Gray bars show published frontier results under their respective evaluation protocols. Full results and settings are in the [paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.11287). ## Acknowledgements The Qwen memory network builds on [DFlash](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash) and [SpecForge](https://github.com/sgl-project/SpecForge). Inference uses [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [Transformers](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers). ## Citation ```bibtex @misc{xia2026remory, title = {Remory: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction}, author = {Xia, Hanchen and Chen, Baoyou and Ge, Yutang and Deng, Naihao and Yang, Senqiao and Dong, Zilong and Yuan, Weihao and Zhu, Siyu}, year = {2026}, eprint = {2610.11287}, archivePrefix = {arXiv}, primaryClass = {cs.CL}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11287} } ``` [Development](docs/development.md) · [MIT License](LICENSE) · [Third-party notices](NOTICES.md)
